newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZIL HINT AT GREATNESS, BUT STUMBLE AT BACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZIL HINT AT GREATNESS, BUT STUMBLE AT BACK.

text.p: Brazil will be looking to repeat their unique achievement of winning the World Cup outside their own continent in France next year.

But exactly a year from the 1998 finals in France -- and what will be the 40th anniversary of their first World Cup win in Sweden in 1958 -- they look more likely to go the way of other potentially great Brazilian sides and stumble before the last hurdle -- victims of the frailty of their defence.

Mario Zagallo's team, who contributed to a superb 3-3 draw with Italy in their Tournoi de France match at Lyon's Gerland stadium on Sunday, have now conceded eight goals in their last three matches in Europe -- hardly the stuff of World Cup winners.
They had to come back in the last quarter of the match from a 3-1 deficit, two of Italy's goals having come from an own goal and a penalty given away by 1994 World Cup central defender Aldair.
The Italians were unlucky not be awarded another penalty for an earlier foul on Italy's match hero Alessandro Del Piero by Aldair's centre-back partner Mauro Silva.

The confusion at the back was reminiscent of Brazil's 1982 World Cup side, who when they needed no more than a draw, still conceded three goals to Italy, the eventual winners, in another memorable clash between the two countries in Barcelona.
Zagallo has pledged himself to guiding Brazil back to their beautiful best, believing he has the players to do so and who would contradict him with gifted 19-year-olds like Denilson?

But a defeat to Italy on Sunday could have brought the wrath of the critical Brazilian press heavily on his back, demanding the more pragmatic approach that landed Carlos Parreira the World Cup in the United States three years ago.
"I'm satisfied because, let's not forget, we hit the post and the crossbar," Zagallo said. "The Brazilian team was transformed in the second half."
"There's no need to explain what they mean to the Brazilian team," he said of his strikers Ronaldo and Romario who scored the second half goals that gave the world champions a draw.
The Italians put tight markers on both players but still suffered as soon as they broke free of the stranglehold.
"With Ronaldo you can't be distracted for a second. We allowed him half a ball and he turned it into a goal," Fabio Cannavaro said.
Italy's Cesare Maldini would also have felt the heat had his side gone down to another defeat in this World Cup dress rehearsal after losing 2-0 to England.

Instead, with the likes of Filippo Inzaghi and Christian Vieri making a impact in the cradle of their international careers, he can maintain his dream of a fourth world title in France where they won their second in 1938.
"We were too tired against England, this evening we recovered our strength and we showed it," Maldini said.
"We have the fortune to have the Italian (serie A) top scorer... He will be a very dangerous forward," he said after Inzaghi was brought down for the penalty then later nearly put Italy 4-1 up.
"It fell badly onto my left (foot) and I didn't manage to give it force and direction," Inzaghi said.

The last time Italy conceded three goals was in a friendly against Sweden in Naples in 1983 which raises possible doubts about their defence while Brazil let in four against Norway in Oslo 11 days ago.
However, Sunday's gem of a match was all about the six goals that were scored. And on that count alone, neither team can be entirely written off for next year either.
